lens: The paradoxical attenuation of metformin's anti-cancer promise in population-level studies, despite potent preclinical efficacy, implicates unappreciated modulators such as metabolic context, dosing regimen, or combinatorial interventions that may define its true therapeutic niche.
known_to_ignore: Metformin's established role as a first-line antidiabetic agent for type 2 diabetes
General anti-proliferative effects of metformin observed in laboratory cancer models
tensions: Tension between metformin's 72% tumor burden reduction in NNK-induced A/J mice [1] and null association with colorectal cancer risk in a large diabetic cohort [2]

Divergent effects of metformin alone versus in combination on inflammatory markers in non-diabetic cancer survivors [8, 9, 10] compared to epidemiological cancer risk reductions in diabetics [11, 13, 14]
gaps: Limited investigation of metformin's efficacy in non-diabetic cancer patients with specific lifestyle interventions like exercise, as seen in [8, 9, 10]
Inadequate exploration of dose-response relationships between preclinical doses (e.g., 150 mg/kg in PDX [4]) and clinical dosing regimens in cancer prevention contexts

theses.title: Context-Dependent Efficacy of Metformin in Cancer Prevention: A Scoping Review Dissecting Preclinical-Clinical Discrepancies
theses.rationale: This review would systematically compare metformin's robust anti-tumor effects in controlled preclinical models with inconsistent epidemiological evidence, identifying key modulating factors like administration route and patient subgroup that could inform targeted clinical trials.

theses.title: Synergistic Potential of Metformin Combinations for Enhanced Anti-Cancer and Anti-Inflammatory Outcomes in Survivorship
theses.rationale: By synthesizing evidence from cell line studies and clinical cohorts on metformin combined with agents like boswellic acid or exercise, this paper could highlight combinatorial strategies that amplify efficacy beyond monotherapy, addressing gaps in survivorship care.

reviewer_objections: Heterogeneity in study designs, populations, and endpoints across preclinical and clinical evidence may undermine causal inferences.
The scoping nature of the review may lack quantitative synthesis, limiting strength of conclusions for clinical translation.
next_extractions: Metformin's impact on lean body mass and muscle mass in non-cancer aging populations, as suggested by alpha hints.
Intratumoral metformin concentration dynamics versus systemic exposure in relation to tumor volume reduction in clinical settings.
